flawed_step: The claim that having the same degree sequence forces two graphs to be isomorphic. The degree sequence does not determine global structure such as whether the graph is connected.
counterexample: G = the 6-cycle C6 on vertices 1..6, with edges 12,23,34,45,56,61. H = two disjoint triangles on vertices a..f, with edges ab,bc,ca,de,ef,fd. Both graphs are simple, have 6 vertices and 6 edges, and every vertex has degree 2, so both degree sequences are (2,2,2,2,2,2). G is connected but H is not: there is no path from a to d. An isomorphism preserves adjacency both ways, so it would carry paths to paths and keep connectivity. So G and H are not isomorphic. (Another way to see it: H contains a triangle and C6 does not.)
assessment_summary: The statement is false. C6 and two disjoint triangles are both simple graphs on 6 vertices where every vertex has degree 2. They are not isomorphic, because one is connected and the other is not (and only one of them contains a triangle).
